findings.finding: The census floor N >= 2 * GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS (30 s) equals the autouse guard's worst-case bounded cost exactly. It leaves no allowance for the test body itself, for any inter-attempt backoff, or for interpreter and fixture overhead. A marker at the floor can therefore still expire if both probes approach their retry bound. This also conflicts with the stated principle that the marker 'must not be tighter than' the guard's cost, because the test needs guard cost plus body time.
findings.location: Approach — census bullet; Acceptance Criteria AC1
scenarios: On a heavily loaded host, a probe that times out twice and succeeds on the third attempt, in both setup and teardown, uses nearly all 30 s before the test body's ~2 s runs. The marker fires again and the flake recurs at a higher threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the floor as `2 * GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS + BODY_HEADROOM_SECONDS`, with the headroom stated in the plan (e.g. 15 s). Raise the three markers to at least that value, e.g. 45 s. In AC1, call it the 'setup+teardown git-probe bound plus headroom'.

tests/_isolation.py:55-60: three attempts, each with timeout=5; the final attempt's TimeoutExpired propagates.
tests/conftest.py:789-793: head() runs in setup and again in teardown.
pyproject.toml:750-753: thread-method expiry calls os._exit(1) and kills the xdist worker.
findings.finding: The census floor `N >= 2 * GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS` (30 s) equals the guard's worst-case cost, so a marker set exactly at the floor leaves no time for the test body. The real worst case is also slightly above 30 s, because subprocess.run kills the child and calls communicate() only after each 5 s timeout. In the worst case the setup probe uses about 15 s, the body (TestClient lifespan plus a fastapi import) takes some time, and the teardown probe needs up to about 15 s more. A 30 s marker then fires inside the teardown probe, and with the thread method that ends the worker via os._exit before the guard's own TimeoutExpired can report the failure properly. That is the same worker-crash pattern the plan sets out to remove. As written, the 'class' rule cannot tell a safe marker from one that still runs into the guard.
findings.location: Approach — census bullet (`N >= 2 * GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * GIT_PROBE_ATTEMPTS`); tests/unit/test_review_bot.py marker value 30
scenarios: A heavily loaded host (load average about 30) where each git start nearly reaches its 5 s attempt bound: setup takes about 15 s, the body about 1 s, and the 30 s marker expires partway through the teardown probe, crashing the worker instead of failing cleanly.

findings.finding: The census's matching rules leave gaps that undercut 'fix the class'. The plan does not say whether the census catches the keyword form `pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)`, the list form `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.timeout(3), ...]`, `pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.timeout(3))`, or an imported alias such as `from pytest import mark` / `@mark.timeout(3)`. It also explicitly ignores non-literal arguments, so `FAST = 3` followed by `@pytest.mark.timeout(FAST)` passes without notice.
findings.location: Approach — census bullet; Testing — Edge bullet
scenarios: A future test written as `@pytest.mark.timeout(timeout=3)` or listed in a `pytestmark = [...]` list reintroduces the same flake, and the census stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Match any Call whose func's dotted name ends in `mark.timeout`, wherever it appears (decorators, Assign values including List/Tuple elements, keyword `marks=`). Read the first positional argument or the `timeout=` keyword. Resolve module-level `Name` constants assigned an int literal, and report unresolved non-literal arguments as offenders instead of ignoring them.

findings.finding: The plan proposes a new whole-tree AST census without saying it will reuse or extend the existing `_timeout_marker_seconds` helper in the same file. That helper already does the literal-argument match: an `ast.Call` whose `func.attr == 'timeout'` and whose first argument is an int or float `ast.Constant`. It stays in use after the change because test_tortoise_nested_signer_run_marker_covers_loaded_cost calls it. A separate walker would put two diverging copies of the literal-marker rule in one module.
scenarios: Someone later widens what counts as a literal (for example a negative constant or a keyword `timeout=` argument) in the census but not in _timeout_marker_seconds, or the other way round, so the named tortoise guard and the census disagree about the same marker.

findings.suggested_fix: Move the decorator check in `_timeout_marker_seconds` into a small predicate, `_literal_timeout_seconds(node: ast.expr) -> int | float | None`. Have `_timeout_marker_seconds` call it, and have the census walk every FunctionDef decorator and every module-level `pytestmark` value (a single Call or the items of a List/Tuple) under tests/ through the same predicate.

The existing helper _timeout_marker_seconds (tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py:37-51) only looks at FunctionDef.decorator_list in module.body. Extending that pattern repeats its blind spots for classes, methods and list-valued pytestmark.
findings.finding: The census only recognises function decorators and a bare `pytestmark = pytest.mark.timeout(N)` assignment. That misses other common ways to attach the same marker that pytest also honours: `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.unit, pytest.mark.timeout(N)]` (the list form this repo already uses for pytestmark), class decorators, and `pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.timeout(N))`. A low marker added in any of these forms gets past the guard the plan relies on to fix the class.
findings.location: Testing — Edge bullet; Approach — census bullet (tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py)
scenarios: A new module declares `pytestmark = [pytest.mark.unit, pytest.mark.timeout(5)]`: the census does not see it, and every test in the module crashes under load.
A test class is decorated with `@pytest.mark.timeout(3)`, or a method inside a class carries it: the census misses it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the census, run `ast.walk(module)` over each parsed file under tests/ and select `ast.Call` nodes whose `func` is an `ast.Attribute` with `attr == 'timeout'` and whose value resolves to `mark` / `pytest.mark`, with `args[0]` an int/float `ast.Constant`. Collect (path, lineno, value) for each value below the floor and report them all in one assertion message.
